name: Deep Research
use_when: The user wants a researched, sourced report or an in-depth briefing on a topic, which requires searching the web across many sources. Examples: 'research the pros and cons of heat pumps', 'write a report on the CPAP market', 'compare these 5 vendors with sources', 'give me a briefing on X for a meeting'.
avoid_when: A quick factual question, a single definition, casual chat, a request to write or edit text that needs no research, or brainstorming and planning that relies on the user's own situation rather than outside sources.
hint: It searches dozens of sources and writes up a full report for you.

name: Code Assistant
use_when: The user wants to build, write, debug, refactor or deploy software: apps, websites, scripts, automations, or multi-file projects. Examples: 'build me a web app that tracks inventory', 'write a Python script to rename these files', 'fix this error in my code'.
avoid_when: Questions about how to use a normal software product, spreadsheet formulas, general tech questions with no code to write, or requests for an SVG or other graphic (even though SVG is technically code).
hint: It's built for coding and can break big projects into pieces and build them for you.

name: Problem Solver
use_when: The user has a complex, open-ended problem that needs careful multi-step reasoning, a detailed plan, a hard decision weighed, or a thoughtful back-and-forth to develop their own ideas. Examples: 'help me plan the staffing for a new location', 'I can't decide between two job offers, help me think it through', 'work through this tricky scheduling problem', 'help me come up with ideas for...'.
avoid_when: Simple questions with a direct answer, tasks that need web research and sources, writing code, generating images, or routine requests like rewriting an email or summarizing a short text.
hint: It's a stronger thinking model that's good at working through hard problems step by step.

name: Image Creation & Editing
use_when: The user wants a picture, photo, illustration, or artwork created, or wants an uploaded image edited (remove or change objects, change style or background, touch up, combine images). Examples: 'make a picture of a cozy cabin in the snow', 'remove the person from this photo', 'turn this into a watercolor'.
avoid_when: The user wants a logo, icon, or scalable/vector graphic or SVG file (use the vector model), or only wants an image described, analyzed or read (OCR) rather than created or changed.
hint: It creates new images and can edit photos you upload.

name: Vector Graphics (SVG)
use_when: The user wants a vector graphic or SVG file: logos, icons, simple illustrations, diagrams or shapes that need to scale cleanly or be edited later. Examples: 'make an SVG logo for my rental', 'design a simple icon set', 'give me a vector illustration of a mountain'.
avoid_when: Photorealistic images, paintings or edits to an uploaded photo (use the image model), or charts and diagrams the user just wants shown in the chat.
hint: It makes a clean, scalable SVG file you can download and edit.
